summary.text: Gabe Amo is the Democratic incumbent for Rhode Island's 1st District, first elected in a November 2023 special election. A Pawtucket native, he worked in the Obama White House, for Governor Gina Raimondo, on Joe Biden's 2020 campaign, and in the Biden White House before running for Congress. His official site lists retirement security, gun violence, climate resilience, reproductive freedom and protecting democracy among his priorities.

paragraphs.text: Amo was born in 1987 and is a native of Pawtucket, Rhode Island; he is the son of a mother from Liberia and a father from Ghana.

He graduated from Moses Brown School in Providence and earned a B.A. in political science from Wheaton College in Norton, Massachusetts, where, according to his official biography, he graduated summa cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa, was student government president and was named a Truman Scholar.
After college he received a Marshall Scholarship to study at the University of Oxford, according to his official biography.
Early in his career Amo served in the Office of Public Engagement and Intergovernmental Affairs for President Barack Obama as a liaison to governors and state government officials.

He was director of public engagement and community affairs for then-Rhode Island Governor Gina Raimondo, serving as her principal advisor to the state's cities and towns, business, labor, advocacy and faith communities.
He then worked as a states-strategy and program advisor on Joe Biden's 2020 presidential campaign.

Under President Biden he served as special assistant to the President and deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs, as principal liaison to mayors and local elected officials.
Amo won the November 7, 2023 special general election for the seat vacated by David Cicilline, defeating Republican Gerry Leonard, and was re-elected in November 2024 over Republican Allen Waters.
He serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee (as vice ranking member), the Science, Space, and Technology Committee (as ranking member of its Environment Subcommittee), and the Budget Committee.
